title: Congestion-aware warmup prober and soft-shedder for dedicated fleets
author: Nina Patel
description: Motivation: Dedicated fleets were experiencing repeated short congestion spikes during cold starts and burst handoffs which caused transient 95th latency regressions. This PR adds a congestion-aware warmup prober together with a soft-shedder policy that temporarily reduces admission for non-critical low-priority tenants while the fleet warms. Design summary: introduce a lightweight probe that samples tail latency and queue depth during warmup windows, compute a congestion score (0-100) with exponential smoothing, and expose signals to the autoscaler and admission controller. When score > threshold the soft-shedder applies a probabilistic reject/backoff on best-effort classes and reduces allowed concurrency for speculative tenants. Configuration: new runtime config under /pkg/autoscaler/config that supports window_ms, smoothing_alpha, congestion_threshold, shed_probability_curve and critical_classes. Telemetry: new metrics redwood_fleet_congestion_score, redwood_warmup_probe_latency_p50/p95, and redwood_soft_shed_rate_by_tier; all exported to Datadog and Prometheus exporters. Rollout: staged rollout with canary pool, default disabled for existing customers; opt-in via dedicated config or Redwood Console toggle. Tests: unit tests for score calculation and shedder logic, integration test that verifies admission behavior against synthetic spike generator, and a small e2e on perf-canary harness. Backwards compatibility: non-breaking by default; configuration flags keep previous behavior unless enabled. Related work: builds on ENG-2134 (warmup telemetry refactor) and ENG-2199 (admission controller refactor).

release_notes: Add a congestion-aware warmup probe and soft-shedder policy for Dedicated fleets. This adds visibility into warmup tail latency and a configurable probabilistic shedding mechanism to protect latency SLOs during cold ramps. Disabled by default; operators can enable via Console toggle or helm values-dedicated. Backwards compatible when disabled.
notes_for_ops: Checklist: 1) Validate new Prometheus metrics are scraped with pool and region labels. 2) When enabling, start with conservative congestion_threshold=60 and smoothing_alpha=0.25. 3) Monitor redwood_fleet_congestion_score and redwood_soft_shed_rate_by_tier. 4) Ensure canary pool is used for first 48h and rollback toggle available.
risk_assessment: Low-medium. New telemetry only and opt-in by default. Main risk is incorrect thresholding causing unnecessary sheds; mitigated by conservative defaults and canary rollout. CPU impact measured <1% in control plane canary tests.
